 How to observe the meeting virtually:

 How to Address the City Council
 Any person who would like to address the Council regarding an item on the agenda,
 please fill out a Speaker's Form and submit it to the City Clerk prior to the agenda item
 you would like to discuss. You may address the Council once per meeting, per public
 comment section of the agenda on only those matters within the Council's jurisdiction.
  Please note that you are not required to complete this form or state your name and
 residence in order to speak. Each person addressing the Council is given up to three
 minutes to speak (with double the time allotted to non-English speakers using a
 translator). The amount of time authorized may be adjusted by the chair. If you wish to
 provide information to the Council, please present the City Clerk with 7 copies. Otherwise,

City Council  Wednesday, March 1, 2023
  your materials will simply be added to the administrative record. If you are attending the
 meeting by phone, please press *9 to "raise your hand." If attending by personal
 computer, please click the "raise your hand" button. Press *6 to un-mute yourself, state
 your name and begin speaking. Please note use of City Council Chamber technology
 equipment to present electronic material during meetings is not allowed.

 In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, if you require a disability-
 related modification or accommodation to participate in this meeting, please contact the
 City Clerk’s Office at (661) 267-5151 at least 72 hours prior to the meeting.

 If you require oral Spanish translation, please contact the City Clerk’s Office at (661) 267-
 5151 at least 72 hours prior to the meeting.

 Your courtesy is requested to help our meetings run smoothly. Please follow these
 simple rules so we can make the best possible use of your time and ours:

  Please refrain from public displays or outbursts, such as unsolicited applause,
  comments, cheering, foul language or obscenities.
  Any disruptive activities that substantially interfere with the ability of the City Council
  to carry out its meeting will not be permitted and offenders will be asked to leave the
  meeting.
  Please turn off/mute your cell phones and mobile devices.

SUBJECT:  RECEIVE AND FILE THE MONTHLY INVESTMENT ACTIVITY
  REPORTS FOR JANUARY 2023

ISSUE
Receive and file the monthly investment activity reports for January 2023.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council accept the monthly investment activity reports
for City of Palmdale and Successor Agency for January 2023.

BACKGROUND
Pursuant to Section 16 of the City of Palmdale and Successor Agency Investment
Policy, the City Treasurer shall prepare and present monthly and quarterly reports on
investments to the City Manager/Executive Director and the City Council/Directors. The
reports shall detail the type of investment, name of the issuer, purchase date, date of
maturity, amount of deposit, and rate of interest. This information shall be provided for
all City and Successor Agency pooled investments, as well as for Certificates of
Participation, Revenue Bonds, Tax Allocation Bonds, Assessment Districts and
Community Facilities District accounts which are managed by outside Fiscal Agents.

The monthly and quarterly reports provide a synopsis of the investment activity for the
City of Palmdale and Successor Agency. The reports provide information on assets,
allocations, average maturities, yields, and book valuations.
The interest rates presented are the most current rates available as of the date of this
report.

The market values presented for pooled City and Successor Agency investments are
based on closing prices for the related investment as of the date of this report. This
information was obtained from the Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg Financial Markets,
Capital Market Finances, or other reliable source of market prices.

Re: Monthly Report on Investments

DISCUSSION
Compliance with Investment Policy

For January, the invested portfolio amount for the City of Palmdale totaled $302,074,175
an increase of $63,019,608 from the previous month, and an increase of $29,968,177
in comparison to last year. The monthly increase is the result of investment purchases,
investments into LAIF and interest earned during the month.

The par value of Successor Agency’s portfolio as of January was $13,595,786. The
balance increased by $6,342,006 from the last month due to a deposit received from LA
County in the Successor Agency bank.

All investments meet criteria appropriate to Section 8 of the Investment Policy. The
portfolios are based on a combination of various investments, including CDs, Corporate
Notes, U.S. Treasury Securities and Government Agency Paper, each adhering to
portfolio percentage limitations.

The Finance Division is the custodian for the City and Successor Agency’s investment
portfolio and follows the three main principles of both entity’s investment policy to 1)
Investment in financial instruments that mitigate the risk of monetary losses stemming
from market fluctuations; 2) Establish and maintain a portfolio that has sufficient liquidity
to allow the City and Successor Agency to meet all anticipated cash requirements; and
3) Seek out investment instruments that provide a competitive market rate of return.

Liquidity

One core approach the Finance Division focuses on, is providing liquidity to measure up
to the City and Successor Agency’s operational requirements. Thus, the Finance
Department is currently investing in two pooled funds, LAIF and CAMP. These are
intended for the daily operational activities, used for economic uncertainties and
maintenance needs. The pooled funds provide a higher liquidity ratio to ensure the City
and Successor Agency meet cash flow requirements.

Total LAIF balance for the City of Palmdale at the end of January is $120,833,729, an
increase of $18,574,948 compared to prior month, due to deposits made to LAIF from
General bank account and interest earned.

Successor Agency LAIF balance at the end of January was $4,458,763, an increase of
$26,046 from prior month due to interest earned.

CAMP’s balance for City of Palmdale at the end of January is $254,063 compared to
December balance of $253,089, a slight increase due to interest earned. The interest
rates presented are the most current rates available as of the date of this report. As of
January 31, 2023, the interest rates for LAIF and CAMP investments were at 2.425

The chart above shows both the Local Agency Investment Fund and California Asset
Management Program’s average monthly yields beginning April 2022 through January
2023.

We anticipate that rates will begin to level off in the upcoming months, considering the
current state of the economy. In recent months, CAMP shows better performance than
LAIF in interest rates. The difference between the performance of the two funds is partly
due to the varying pool characteristics. CAMP’s portfolio composition is much more
subject to market volatility, resulting in performance variation.

Diversity
The Finance Division aims to diversify the investment portfolios to avoid incurring
unreasonable and avoidable risks regarding specific security types or individual financial
institutions.

City of Palmdale and Successor Agency’s investment portfolios remain strongly
diversified. The monthly and quarterly reports include all investments held by both
entities and current book values as of January 31, 2023.

It is anticipated that both the City of Palmdale and Successor Agency will have sufficient
moneys to meet its expenditure requirements for the next 6 months as we continue to
monitor any financial impact due to the Coronavirus pandemic and the current economic
conditions and the impact on interest rates.

DATE:  MARCH 1, 2023
TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL
FROM:  PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT
  CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM DIVISION
DISTRICT:  1
SUBJECT:  APPROVE CONSULTANT AGREEMENT WITH MNS ENGINEERS
  INC. FOR PN 669, SR138(SR14) & 10th STREET WEST WIDENING,
  IN THE AMOUNT OF $191,800.

ISSUE
Approve Consultant Agreement with MNS Engineers, Inc. for PN 669, SR138(SR14) &
10th Street West Widening, in the amount of $191,800.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve Agreement No. A-8233, with MNS Engineers, Inc. for PN 669,
  SR138(SR14) & 10th Street West Widening, in the amount of $191,800.

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute Agreement No. A-8233,
  with MNS Engineers, Inc. including minimal and/or non-substantive changes.

BACKGROUND
The City of Palmdale identified the need for owner’s representation services for PN 669
SR138(SR14) & 10th West Widening. In January 2023, MNS Engineers, Inc, an on-call
engineering consultant, submitted a proposal to provide project management services
and constructability review for this project. Due to current limited staffing, hiring a
consultant to provide management services will ensure that the project continues forward.
This project will improve the level of service by increasing capacity, reducing congestion,
and improving overall operations and safety along 10th Street West, including its access
to the Antelope Valley Mall and the Sierra Commons Shopping Area.

DISCUSSION
The consultant will act as the City’s representative for this project. The following scope
of work provides a brief description of tasks and responsibilities that MNS Engineers Inc.
will provide to the city:
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Agreement No. A-8233
March 1, 2023
Page 2

1. Project Management Services-MNS Engineers, Inc. will provide Project Management
Services to the City to oversee the timely delivery of the 10th Street West Project through
the bidding phase. MNS will provide services necessary to verify the project meets City
standards and expectations.

2. Constructability Review – MNS Engineers, Inc. will perform a Constructability Review
of the project plans and specifications and provide comments and recommendations
based upon construction experience and project understanding. The review will include
review of the supporting documents and construction estimate. During the constructability
review, MNS Engineers, Inc. will identify missing details, time considerations,
deficiencies, and potential coordination issues. MNS Engineers, Inc. will provide a
constructability report to the city and discuss findings with the city. This report will include
a listing of specification review comments referenced by specification section and page
number. Review comments of the drawings listing sheet number and appropriate detail
reference.

made and entered into by and between the City of Palmdale a public body corporate
and politic, (hereinafter called “CITY”) and MNS Engineers, Inc. (hereinafter called
“PROJECT DESIGNER”). This Contract shall become effective on the date of the last
signatory.

  RECITALS

  WHEREAS, City desires to engage PROJECT DESIGNER to perform certain
technical and professional services, as provided herein, in connection with that
certain project identified as PN 669 SR138 (SR14) & 10th Street West Widening.

  WHEREAS, PROJECT DESIGNER represents that PROJECT DESIGNER
has the expertise and is qualified to perform the services described in this Contract
and is duly registered under the laws of the State of California.

  WHEREAS, PROJECT DESIGNER desires to accept such engagement.

NOW, THEREFORE, the parties agree as follows:

1  DESCRIPTION OF WORK

1.1  The City hereby engages PROJECT DESIGNER, and PROJECT DESIGNER
accepts such engagement, to perform the following design professional services in a
manner satisfactory to CITY:

PROJECT DESIGNER shall act as the CITY’s representative for this project. The
following scope of work provides a brief description of tasks and responsibilities that
PROJECT DESIGNER shall provide to the CITY:

1. Project Management Services - PROJECT DESIGNER shall provide Project
Management Services to the CITY to oversee the timely delivery of the 10th Street
West Project through the bidding phase. MNS shall provide services necessary to
verify the project meets CITY standards and expectations. The PROJECT
DESIGNER shall:
-Serve as the CITY's Project Manager for project delivery through the Bidding Phase
-Oversee completion of the Bid Package by CITY consultants
-Coordinate and communicate with the CITY
-Oversee the implementation of the project environmental into the plans,
specifications, and estimate (PSE)
-Ensure the project PSE documents conform with project funding guidelines
-Manage CITY consultants through R/W acquisition phase
-Conduct project funding review and alternative funding strategies

  Concord - Document ID: generated after first signature  1-15
 -Conduct overall program management of the project

2. Constructability Review - PROJECT DESIGNER shall perform a Constructability
Review of the project plans and specifications and provide comments and
recommendations based upon construction experience and project understanding.
The review shall include review of the supporting documents and construction
estimate. During the constructability review, PROJECT DESIGNER shall identify
missing details, time considerations, deficiencies, and potential coordination issues.
PROJET DESIGNER shall:
-Verify the plans and specifications are unambiguous, comprehensive, consistent,
and buildable
-Verify items of work have adequately defined scope and pay mechanisms.
-Review permit, utility, and geotechnical provisions
-Review project working days and staging
PROJECT DESIGNER shall provide a constructability report to and discuss finding
with CITY. This report shall include a listing of specification review comments
referenced by specification section and page number. Review comments of the
drawing shall list sheet number and appropriate detail reference.

1.2  Project deliverables shall be reviewed and approved by CITY to determine
acceptable completion. CITY shall have the right to review and inspect the work
during the course of its performance at such times as may be specified by CITY.

1.3  PROJECT DESIGNER shall not accept any change of scope, or change in
contract provisions, unless issued in writing, as a contract change order or
amendment and signed by CITY. Any extensions of time must be mutually agreed
upon in writing and executed by both parties.

1.4  CITY shall provide to PROJECT DESIGNER, without charge, all data,
program information, including reports, records, maps, and other information, now in
CITY’s possession, which may facilitate the timely performance of the work.

2  CITY PROJECT MANAGER

To provide the design professional services required by this Contract, PROJECT
DESIGNER shall act under the authority and approval of a Project Manager
appointed by the Director of Public Works/designee. The City Project Manager will
oversee the work under this Contract, assist PROJECT DESIGNER with any
necessary information, audit billings, and approve payments. PROJECT DESIGNER

Resolution entitled “Annexation 20-101” with the County Sanitation District No. 20 of

BACKGROUND
In accordance with the Revenue and Tax Code (Sections 99 and 99.01) any time there
is a jurisdictional change, the County Auditor is required to adjust the allocation of
property tax revenue for local agencies whose service area or service responsibility
would be altered by the jurisdictional change. This adjustment, or “Tax Sharing
Agreement” determines the distribution of the annual property tax among all affected
public agencies and special districts. In this case, the Pilot Gas Station and Antelope
Valley Swap Meet located near the northwest corner of Pearblossom Highway and
State Route 138 has requested annexation into the County Sanitation District (CSD)
No. 20.

DISCUSSION
In the attached letter dated November 30, 2022, the County Sanitation District has
requested that the City of Palmdale enter into a tax sharing agreement for the
annexation of parcel numbers 3051-019-030, 3051-019-112, and 3051-021-022 as
shown in Exhibit A, also known as the Pilot Gas Station and Antelope Valley Swap
Meet.

The execution of the attached Joint Resolution will approve the tax sharing agreement
by the City for the annexation of the subject property into the County Sanitation District
No. 20 boundary. All public agencies and special districts that receive property tax
revenues for this parcel execute and are a party to the same resolution.

Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-010 authorizing
the Mayor to execute the Joint Tax Sharing Resolution entitled Annexation No. 20-101
with the County Sanitation District No. 20 for the Pilot Gas Station and Antelope Valley
Swap Meet.

FISCAL IMPACT
The current property tax share ratio for the City of Palmdale within the area of the Pilot
Gas Station and Antelope Valley Swap Meet properties is 0.066247854 (6.6247%)

ISSUE
Adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-012, a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
Palmdale approving the application for Local Streets and Roads Funds authorized under
Article 8 of the Transportation Development Act.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-012 for the purpose of approving the application
  for Local Streets and Roads Funds authorized under Article 8 of the Transportation
  Development.

  2. Authorize the Director of Public Works as the City’s authorized signature and
  designated contact person for allocation of Transportation Development Act (TDA)
  funds for street and road improvements.

BACKGROUND
Transportation Development Act (TDA) Article 8 funds are intended to fund unmet transit
needs in areas outside the Metro service area, i.e., North Los Angeles County and Santa
Catalina Island. However, if there are no unmet transit needs in these areas that are
reasonable to meet, the Article 8 funds can be used for streets and roads expenditures.
A public hearing must be held each year in each of the eligible areas to determine
whether there are unmet transit needs and whether they can be met using an allocation
of Article 8 funds. Since the City of Palmdale has met its unmet public transportation
needs through an agreement with Antelope Valley Transit Authority (AVTA) to provide

Page 2

public transportation in the City of Palmdale, the allocation of Transportation
Development Act funds will be used for minor street and road improvements.

Article 8 claims are filed by the Cities of Avalon, Lancaster, Palmdale, Santa Clarita and
the County (for the unincorporated area in the North Los Angeles County and
unincorporated Santa Catalina Island outside the Metro service area). In expending
Article 8 monies for Local Streets and Roads purposes, the State Controller's Guidelines
on Gas Tax Expenditures (Sections 100-400) are used as general guidance for eligible
use of funds.

DISCUSSION
The Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (Metro) adopted the FY
2022-23 Transportation Development Act (TDA) Article 8 allocations on June 23, 2022.
To claim and receive funds the City must submit the claim forms and approved resolution
no later than June 30, 2023. Staff recommends that the City Council approve Resolution
No. 2023-012 approving the application for Local Streets and Roads Funds authorized
under Article 8 of the Transportation Development.

FISCAL IMPACT
Annual allocation of TDA Article 8 revenue for FY 2022-23 in the amount of $8,658,196
and estimated interest income of $10,000 is budgeted and will be used for local streets
and roads projects. To ensure that TDA funds are spent in a timely manner and that
interest earned on these funds are accrued, allocated and expended consistently with
the original allocations, local jurisdictions can claim each year only the funds needed for
expenditures anticipated within the fiscal year.

ISSUE

provide Certificate In Applied Positive Psychology Program in an amount not to exceed

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve Agreement No. A-8208 with The Wellbeing Lab dba Louis Alloro, LLC to
  provide Certificate in Applied Positive Psychology Program (CAPP) in an amount
  not to exceed $275,000; and,
  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute Agreement No. A-8208
  with The Wellbeing Lab dba Louis Alloro, LLC, including minimal and/or non-
  substantiative changes.

BACKGROUND
In 2021, in response to the community’s expressed strong interest in making wellbeing
resources more widely available, the City offered the Certificate in Applied Positive
Psychology Program (CAPP).

CAPP provides guidance and support in helping teams thrive even in the face of ongoing
turbulence, uncertainty, disappointment, depression, or worse. Research shows that
wellbeing, the ability to feel good and function effectively, helps us create the workplaces,
schools, organizations, and communities that are also optimally functioning. The program
provides intelligent, evidence-based insights and tools that deliver measurable results.

Over 35 community members comprised of residents, medical providers, schools, non-
profits participated in the first CAPP cohort and executed on impact projects such as:
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Approve Agreement A-8208 with The Wellbeing Lab dba Louis Alloro, LLC
March 1, 2023
Page 2

Welcome Home Ceremony for Vietnam Veterans: a celebration for veterans whose
original homecoming was an extremely negative experience. This day-long event
featured 1960s inspired music and food and helped our beloved Veterans feel like heroes,
fostering new neural networks around our gratitude and appreciation for their service;

Healing Garden: a public park and garden space built by the cohort for Veterans and
other community members to have healing experiences;

The Senior Wellbeing Experience: a half-day experiential workshop focused on the
mental, physical, and emotional wellbeing of seniors, and provided an opportunity for
social engagement within a “safe space,” as one way to combat the senior loneliness
epidemic;

You Women Matter: a day-long event that offered a hand-up for unhoused women in the
Antelope Valley to experience a state of wellbeing, be nourished and counseled, as well
as connected to resources to restore them to a state of wellbeing in all areas of their lives;
i.e., physically, mentally, emotionally, spiritually, relationally, and financially;

Reinvigorating Entrepreneurs Workshop: a day-long experience of workshops on
wellbeing, post-traumatic growth, strengths, and resources to support thriving local
entrepreneurs and business;

Zen Academy: a once-per-week class held prior to the school day for 5th–8th grade
students, focusing on managing emotions, leaning positive coping skills, working on
social skills and building positive relationships; and,

Strong Families and Youth: a team dedicated to working with high school students to
identify strengths and crate psychological safety to explore challenges and triumphs of
being a teen.

Based on the participants’ positive experience throughout the program and their
continued desire to conduct wellbeing efforts in the community, the City seeks to offer an
additional cohort. The program meets the community’s desired interest in making
wellbeing resources more widely available.

  SCOPE OF WORK
The Certificate In Applied Positive Psychology (CAPP) program is an eight-month evidence-
based, blended learning program for people who want an impactful, evidence-based,
systems-oriented approaches for improving wellbeing across their entire community. One
that goes beyond just ‘knowing’ better, to truly, with confidence, ‘doing’ better.

The course is organized around renowned University of Pennsylvania’s Professor Martin
Seligman’s (2011) PERMAH model: Positive Emotions, Engagement, Relationships,
Meaning, Accomplishment, and Health.

Through CAPP, participants will learn to:

  •  Make the science of wellbeing joyful, accessible and actionable in their own lives
  •  Help others thrive, even in times of struggle, and be better equipped with collaborative
  solutions to some of our shared social challenges
  •  Articulate a clear business case for wellbeing by sharing the social and economic
  impact wellbeing behaviors have on their workplace, school campus, or entire AV
  community
  •  Design psychologically safe spaces for teams, groups, and families to playfully
  experiment with more effective and joyful ways to support each other’s wellbeing,
  even in the midst of struggle.
  •  Co-create thriving workplaces, schools, and communities by taking a strengths-based
  approach to creating positive changes that fuel belonging, build trust, bolster
  resilience, and improve health and wellbeing outcomes.
  •  Evaluate the collective impact of our efforts at an individual, team, family, and
  organizational or community level using our proprietary, validated PERMAH Wellbeing
  Survey

CAPP is delivered in a hybrid online/onsite (live) training, led by highly positive psychology
teachers and coaches, and includes:

  •  Six (6) – 1.5 day long face-to-face, deep dive, intensive workshops, onsite in Palmdale,
  CA spread over six months (1.5 days per month);
  •  15 - 90-minute weekly, live, online coaching sessions;
  •  One-on-one coaching as needed or requested for all participants;
  •  Two (2) months - extended coaching calls to execute community impact projects; and,
  •  Proposed Course Timeline
  Onsite 1: March 23-24
  Onsite 2: April 20-21
  Onsite 3: May 18-19
  Onsite 4: June 22-23
  Onsite 5: July 27-28
  No Onsite: August
  Onsite 6: September 7-8
  No Onsite: October & November – participants working on Impact Projects
  Final Showcase & Graduation celebration: December 7-8

  1
 CAPP is supported by a customized online training platform which enables champions to
have lifelong access to one easy-to-use source of all the program materials, session
recordings, playbooks and includes the following bonus resources:

  •  Curricular Resources – An online learning portal provides lifetime access o f
  recordings, slides and detailed learning manuals packed with resources from each
  workshop. In addition, real-time chat forums are available to ensure participants can
  easily share their learnings on a dedicated Slack channel for Antelope Valley.

  •  Done-For-You Tools – Participants will have access to a wealth of beautiful and
  impactful done-for them tools, including, wellbeing presentations, wellbeing
  conversation guides, wellbeing check-in instructions, and step-by-step team
  activities to help people discover and develop their strengths and build psychological
  safety. Champions will be able to use (and re-brand if desired) these tools to
  immediately share what they are learning and support their impact projects.

  •  Podcast Series with The World’s Leading Positive Psychology Researchers –
  Champions will be able to hear from the world’s leading positive psychology
  researchers about their latest findings when it comes to caring for wellbeing in
  workplaces and grab cheat sheets summarizing their research and ways it can be
  applied in workplaces, schools, and across the entire region.

RECRUITMENT
To ensure equity, CONTRACTOR will take an intentional approach to the recruitment of
diverse participants representing all of Antelope Valley. CONTRACTOR will assist the
CITY in reaching out to the following groups:

  •  Industry HR departments;

  •  Community health centers and hospitals leaders;

  •  School districts, particularly to social workers and other mental health professionals
  working in these settings;

  •  County mental health practitioners and officers; and,

  •  Non-profit organization leaders in public service, mental health, education, veteran
  affairs, the unhoused, women services, foster youth and children and families’
  services.

CONTRACTOR shall work with CITY to recruit participants and:
  • Help CITY identify the appropriate individuals in each of the sectors mentioned in the
  previous section;
  •  Write scripts for phone calls, and collaborate with the CITY and other organizations
  who may have direct contact with potential recruitment sites;
  •  Provide testimonials from the first cohort participants;
  •  Develop a flyer describing the curriculum, dates the class will be offered, benefits to
  participants, and to the community, including past impact projects; and,
  •  Describe opportunities to contribute to the personal wellbeing and that of families and
  the community.

  2
 RETENTION

To retain participants throughout the duration of the program CONTRACTOR shall:

  •  Suggest requiring a sliding-scale fee from each participant (self-funded or from
  sponsoring agency (their workplace or faith community, etc.), in combination with the
  scholarship from the CITY, to ensure everyone has personal accountability for starting
  what they finish
  •  Build community among participants to ensure people get to know each other and
  develop trust and rapport
  •  Establish initial agreements and commitments as members of the group
  •  Develop the skills for building strong teams working through different perspectives,
  personalities, and working styles
  •  Ensure that each class is interactive and participants can work in small groups and
  learn from and with each other
  •  Provide in-depth guidance for each module content and assignments
  •  Ensure that all participants are familiar with accessing the digital resources offered
  such as the wellbeing toolbox, articles and videos
  •  Offer coaching throughout the course to individuals and groups
  •  Pair participants up with class members and members of the previous cohort (2021-
  2022) as a way to increase social support
  •  Provide opportunity and support to practice wellbeing skills in class and in participants
  daily life
  •  Be a source of joy, inspiration and energy – be positive energizers

CONTRACTOR shall leverage graduates from the first CAPP class to serve as mentors and
offer social support to the current participants.

CONTRACTOR shall set up accountability buddies within the class, so participants have
an additional layer of protection.

  3
 EVALUATION
CONTRACTOR shall provide quality, meaningful and timely data-based insights to help
make intelligent decisions and effective wellbeing investments. CONTRACTOR shall
gather qualitative interviews, quantitative measures, like the PERMAH Wellbeing Survey,
and other existing data sources for analysis and reporting to workplace, school, and
community clients.

PERMAH Wellbeing Survey

The PERMAH Wellbeing Survey provides immediate, confidential and actionable insights
for workplaces, schools and entire communities by providing the following:

  •  Data collection - the survey may be shared online to whoever, whenever, and as
  often as necessary. Done-for-you emails make it easy to secure people’s
  participation. CONTRACTOR’s research coaches are available to handle any
  obstacles encountered during data collection (i.e. COVID lockdowns). In addition,
  pen and paper versions are available and CONTRACTOR’s team shall make it as
  easy as possible for CITY to upload and track these results in the database.

  •  Wellbeing Reports - Participants who complete the survey shall immediately
  receive a personalized wellbeing report with small, every day, evidence-based
  ideas to improve wellbeing.

  •  Done-For-You Reporting & Data Warehousing – CITY can track aggregated, de-
  identified survey participation and results in real-time during data collection.
  CONTRACTOR shall gather data and prepared a PDF report of results that can
  easily be shared with stakeholders. CONTRACTOR shall provide a .csv file
  automatically each time the CITY gathers data for easy storage and reference. If
  required accumulated data can be stored in a data warehouse for easy future
  access and analysis.

  •  Deeper Dive Analysis & Debriefs – If requested, CONTRACTOR’s research coach
  may further analysis or report across time periods, aggregated groups, or around
  specific topics to assist in producing additional analysis, reporting and providing
  debriefs as required.

  •  Wellbeing Research Coaches – CONTRACTOR’s wellbeing research coaches shall
  be available to help guide CITY’s survey design, data collection and analysis.

As part of the CAPP program, CITY shall have access to CONTRACTOR’s PERMAH
Wellbeing Survey for 12 months and can access reporting that shows the wellbeing of the
community in comparison to the data collected in 2021. These cross sectional touch points
can inform the impact projects coming out of the CAPP class.

SUBJECT:  APPROVE A DESIGN BUILD AGREEMENT, FOR AN ENERGY
  SERVICES CONTRACT, WITH SCHNEIDER ELECTRIC, IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $8,491,602 FOR A CONSTRUCTION TERM OF THREE
  YEARS
SUBJECT
Approve a design build agreement, for an Energy Services Contract, with Schneider
Electric in the amount of $8,491,602 for a construction term of three years.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve Agreement No. A-8161 with Schneider Electric for energy services in the
  amount of $8,491,602.

  2. Approve the reallocation of $8,491,602 from several applicable budgets for the first
  year of projects.

  3. Authorize staff to execute all documents necessary to obtain $1.85 million in zero
  percent interest loans through Southern California Edison’s On Bill Financing
  Program and the Southern California Regional Energy Network’s Revolving
  Savings Fund program.

  4. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute Agreement No. A-8161,
  with Schneider Electric, including minimal and/or non-substantive changes.

BACKGROUND
In August 2021, Palmdale issued a bid solicitation utilizing Government Code 4217 to
select an Energy Services Company, ESCO, that would develop and implement building
improvements to reduce energy and related operation costs in City facilities. As a result
of this competitive qualification process, Schneider Electric was selected to perform an
investment grade audit in collaboration with Palmdale staff. The purpose of the audit
was to evaluate City operations at almost all City facilities to determine the use of utilities
and to identify any efficiencies that could provide value to the City’s operations while
reducing utility expenditures.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Approval of Agreement A-8161
Date of Meeting: March 1, 2023
Page 2

After extensive reviews of utility bills, thorough inspections of facilities, and interviews
with City staff members, Schneider developed their Phase 1 guaranteed energy and
water savings projects for the City. The scope of work includes a wide range of benefits
to the City, including, but not limited to: realizing utility savings, replacing equipment
operating beyond its serviceable lifespan and overdue for replacement, and helping the
City to realize added savings and benefits beyond utility savings. Schneider Electric was
able to design and implement energy conservation, energy efficiency, energy generation
and other energy related capital improvement services pursuant to California
Government Code Section 4217.10 et seq.

DISCUSSION
After almost a year of research, interviews, site walks, and analysis; Schneider Electric
has completed an extensive investment grade analysis. With the audit complete,
Schneider has prepared an outline of several projects recommended for City facilities and
the justifications are listed below:
   Several facilities have HVAC units that are operating well beyond their
  recommended useful lives of 15 years (42 units). Although Maintenance has been
  able to maintain the units, they have the potential to eventually fail, leading to
  expensive repairs and loss of productivity.
   Some City buildings have an assortment of building control solutions that monitor
  the heating and air systems. Many of which have obsolete systems where
  components are no longer available, leading again to the potential for the loss of
  productivity (four buildings).
   Several City facilities still have fluorescent and other similar technology lights. With
  the help of the Southern California Regional Energy Network’s (SoCalREN’s)
  Revolving Savings Fund and California Public Utility Commission’s (CPUC) On Bill
  Financing program, the City will be able to retrofit with Light Emitting Diode (LED)
  lights. The proposed LED lights will be more efficient, provide higher quality light,
  and require less maintenance.
   With the ongoing drought, water conservation is of the utmost importance.
  However, by being an early implementor of smart irrigation technologies, the City’s
  current irrigation infrastructure is nearing being phased out. The controllers need
  to be replaced before they become obsolete (20 controllers).

Overall, Phase 1 will encompass:
   Lighting Efficiency Projects
  o Interior Lighting Retrofits (5 sites)
  o Exterior Lighting Retrofits (5 sites)
  o Sports Field LED Retrofits (2 sites)
   HVAC and Controls
  o HVAC Replacements (6 sites)
  o HVAC and Lighting Controls Converted to Automated Logic Controllers (6
  sites)

  Internal

    Other
  o Irrigation Controllers, Booster Pumps, and Master Valves and Flow Sensors
  Upgraded or Replaced (22 sites)
  o Retrofit of several streetlights to LED lights.

Future phase(s) of Schneider Electric’s investment grade audit and development will
address future needs at the City’s Maintenance Facility based on changes in policies
affecting Maintenance Operations, requirements related to air quality and fleet
electrification as well a potential microgrid projects that are potentially eligible for
upcoming grant opportunities. Future phases will involve an amendment to their
contract that will be brought forward for Council approval in the future. Council will
receive an outline of the proposed work for subsequent fiscal year(s) through the regular
budget process. The projects that will commence with the first phase were selected
based on their respective funding sources.

Staff is recommending the agreement and first phase of projects for City Council approval,
with the associated building and facilities improvements. Once all projects identified in
Schneider’s first phase of their Investment Grade Audit are completed, it is anticipated

FISCAL IMPACT
This project spans multiple fiscal years where several grant and incentive programs are
contributing to the full payment of the project. The fixed/firm fee associated with the
contract amount is $8.49 million. It is anticipated the City will save $10.1 million
throughout the life of the proposed projects (without factoring in added savings from
decreased maintenance and proactively performing retrofits on facilities prior to
equipment failure). With the ARPA and Library grant funding contribution of $5,275,000
total, the City of Palmdale is only investing $3,216,600 towards this project, with a 20-
year total savings of $10,054,868, or net savings after investment of $6,838,266.

For the remainder of FY 2022-2023, the budget for Schneider Electric projects will be:
   $4,850,000 in ARPA funds (G0095158).

As outlined above, through the City’s work with Schneider Electric, the City is looking to
obtain $1.85 million in zero percent interest loans. Both the CPUC through Southern
California Edison (On Bill Financing Program) and the SoCalREN (Revolving Savings
Fund Program) offer the loans for energy efficiency projects. Repayment of the loans are
based on savings, where, for example, if one of the measures is estimated to realize
$1,000 in utility savings per month, the loan repayment amount will be set at $1,000 per
month. Once paid off, the City will realize the savings in its entirety.

Additionally, it should be noted that the ARPA funds are from a Federal Grant; the
Anaverde Streetlights Assessment District Reserves are dedicated funds that can only
be used in that Assessment District for streetlight related projects; and the Library Grant
Project budget is specifically for the Library project. Staff worked closely with Schneider
Electric to minimize costs to the City’s General Fund.

DISCUSSION
The proposed Ordinance, if adopted, will change the regular meeting frequency of the
City Council of the City of Palmdale to twice a month instead of the current once a month.
The proposed Ordinance would change the meeting dates to the first and third
Wednesday of each month except in January and July where regular meetings will be
held on the second and third Wednesday of those months. The Ordinance, if adopted,
will also change the start time of the regular meeting to 5:00 p.m. with Closed Session, if
any, being held immediately following the regular meeting which is in line with the survey
results received.

The proposed changes to the Palmdale Municipal Code Section 2.08.040 by this
Ordinance are as follows:

2.08.040 Regular meeting day, time and place.

Regular meetings of the City Council will be held on the first and third Wednesday of each
month except in January and July where regular meetings will be held on the second
Wednesday of those months. Meetings of the City Council shall be held at 38300 Sierra
Highway, Suite B, Palmdale, California, at 5:00 p.m. If all matters on the agenda for any
regular meeting have not been considered by the City Council by the hour of 10:30 p.m.,
or such earlier or later time as may be fixed by a majority vote of the City Council, then
the regular meeting may be adjourned to the next succeeding Wednesday, at the same
time and at the same location, unless a different day, time or location is specified in the
order of adjournment. When so adjourned, each adjourned meeting shall be a regular
meeting for all purposes. Notice of all meetings of the City Council, whether regular,
adjourned, special or emergency, will be given in the manner required by statute. When
a regular Wednesday meeting of the City Council falls on a national or state holiday and
City offices are scheduled to be closed, then such meeting shall not be held and will be
deemed adjourned for all purposes with no further action required by the City Council or
the City Clerk except such written notices of adjournment as may be required by law. The
ordinance codified in this section shall take effect 30 days after adoption.

The budget serves as the city’s financial plan for the fiscal year beginning July 1 through
June 30. It defines the City’s priorities for the provision of services to the community.

On June 29, 2022, the City Council approved the FY 2022-23 Annual Operating and
Maintenance Budget and Capital Improvement Program. Since budget adoption,
financial and operational needs not accommodated by the current budget have been
identified and need to be incorporated into the FY 2023 Budget. This is necessary to
better reflect program costs for the benefit of the community.
Carryforwards of encumbrances and unspent funds are included from the previous fiscal
year for review and approval as well. Encumbrances are funds that are assigned to a
Purchase Order and completion of the purchase or services have not been completed
in the current fiscal year therefore need to be carried forward for use in the next fiscal
year. Unspent budget funds are carried forward by approval of the City Manager when
projects or purchases are delayed for reasons beyond the City’s control.

Personnel

In efforts to address the growing needs of the community and organization, an
organizational restructure of the City Manager and City Council offices would provide the
opportunity to strategically align staff and department roles with the workload demanded
to meet those needs. The restructure focuses on the future of the organization,
developing policies, procedures, internal controls, segregation of duties and ultimately
aligns roles to be responsible for overseeing integral initiatives and special projects for
the City.

Staff requests two (2) Deputy City Manager positions, one (1) additional Executive
Assistant position, one (1) City Council Liaison position.

These positions would provide the City Manager Department and City Council office with
a strong and enhanced level of leadership and expertise to carry out the increased
workload and responsibilities. It is anticipated that these pressures continue to increase
as the City continues to create new programs and initiatives utilizing various outside
funding sources. It is in the best interest of the City to provide staff with an achievable
work-life balance to ensure staff wellbeing and the long-term success of the City. The two
(2) Deputy City Manager positions would replace current vacant positions of Director of
Operations and Director of Neighborhood Services, therefore there is no fiscal impact
associated with those positions. The Executive Assistant and City Council Liaison
positions would have no fiscal impact in FY 2023 but would have an ongoing fiscal impact
of $241,150 in FY 2024, subject to cost of living and merit increases, consistent with
general positions.

Staff also requests one (1) Economic Development Manager position. This position was
previously funded, however remained vacant for a period of time as the department re-
organized. It is now being recommended to fund this position and fill based on the need
for support of the Visit Palmdale program and increased focus on economic development
priorities. Visit Palmdale has approved to fund $50,000 of this position in the first year,
and staff will be requesting a longer term commitment from Visit Palmdale upon approval.
The fiscal impact for FY 2023 will be minimal, if any. The position would likely be filled in
late FY 2023 or early FY 2024. The ongoing fiscal impact of this position is $211,200 in
FY 2024, subject to cost of living and merit increases, consistent with general positions.
